aciklama: Learn the basic principles of good character in light of the Quran and authentic hadiths.

kartlar.icerik:
Good character is a way of being a servant of Allah that brings together respect for Allah, justice toward people, kindness in speech, mercy in the heart, and honesty in behavior.

Merely appearing polite is not enough to have good character. Good character is shown by speaking truthfully, looking down on no one, managing anger, honoring trusts, being forgiving, and not harming others.

A Muslim's character is not separate from acts of worship; it is the fruit of worship reflected in daily life.
kartlar.vurgu: Good character is iman reflected in behavior

kartlar.baslik: Why Is Good Character So Important?
kartlar.icerik:
The Prophet ﷺ said that good character is one of the heaviest things on the scales on the Day of Judgment. This shows that good character is not merely a matter of social politeness, but a great asset for the Hereafter.

A person of good character is not simply someone who gets along well with others, but someone who strives to remain on the path of servitude that pleases Allah. Good character makes a person trustworthy in the eyes of others and raises their rank in the sight of Allah.

Sources: Tirmidhi 2003, Abu Dawud 4799.
kartlar.vurgu: Good character is a great virtue of servitude that weighs heavily on the scales

kartlar.baslik: The Messenger of Allah Is the Finest Example
kartlar.icerik:
The Quran states that the Messenger of Allah is an excellent example for believers. Therefore, when learning good character, the standard is the example of the Messenger of Allah, not whatever is fashionable among people.

The hadiths also tell us that the Prophet ﷺ did not use bad or obscene language and that the best people are those with the best character. His Sunnah teaches a life of mercy, patience, trustworthiness, moderation, and dignity.

Sources: al-Ahzab 33:21; Bukhari 3559.
kartlar.vurgu: The standard for character is the example of the Messenger of Allah

kartlar.icerik:
The Quran states that Allah commands justice, ihsan, and helping relatives, and forbids indecency, wrongdoing, and transgression.

Justice means giving everyone their due. Ihsan means going beyond giving people their due and completing a good deed with excellence. A believer of good character does not violate anyone's rights and, when given the opportunity, goes further in doing good.

Character is founded on standards, not personal pleasure. Even if we find an action pleasing, it cannot be considered good character if it involves injustice.

Source: an-Nahl 16:90.
kartlar.vurgu: The backbone of good character is justice, ihsan, and avoiding transgression

kartlar.icerik:
The Prophet ﷺ said that truthfulness leads a person to righteousness, and righteousness leads to Paradise, while lying leads to wrongdoing and the Fire.

Truthfulness is more than simply not lying. Keeping one's word, honoring trusts, and not giving incomplete or distorted information are also parts of truthfulness. Trust is one of the most visible fruits of good character.

A Muslim does not use lies for short-term gain, because even a small corruption in speech can, over time, corrupt a person's character.

Source: Bukhari 6094.
kartlar.vurgu: Truthfulness elevates character, while lying corrupts a person

kartlar.icerik:
The Messenger of Allah advised that whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should speak good or remain silent.

The tongue is the outward door through which the iman, anger, arrogance, or mercy in the heart is expressed. Good character requires abandoning idle, hurtful, and rude speech, as well as words that cause discord. A true word can be an act of charity, while a wrong word can cause lasting hurt.

Before speaking, it is helpful to ask three questions: Is it true? Is it necessary? Is it kind?

Source: Bukhari 6475.
kartlar.vurgu: Speak good; if there is no good to say, remain silent

kartlar.baslik: Avoiding Mockery, Insults, and Offensive Nicknames
kartlar.icerik:
The Quran forbids one group from mocking another, people from finding fault with one another, and calling one another by offensive nicknames.

Looking down on someone is sometimes disguised as a joke, but a joke that hurts someone's feelings is not good character. Making people's faults a source of entertainment is a serious wrong in the sight of Allah, even if it stems from a desire to appear powerful in social settings.

A believer rises by valuing others, not by humiliating them.

Source: al-Hujurat 49:11.
kartlar.vurgu: Belittling others is injustice, not good character

kartlar.icerik:
The Quran warns against negative suspicion, searching for people's hidden faults, and backbiting. Backbiting is saying something about a fellow believer behind their back that they would dislike.

Assuming the worst about someone's intentions without evidence, investigating people's private lives online, or talking about them behind their backs are behaviors that darken the heart. Good character means being able to restrain one's tongue and curiosity.

A person who seeks to correct their own faults rather than focus on the faults of others progresses more quickly on the path of good character.

Source: al-Hujurat 49:12.
kartlar.vurgu: Negative suspicion, spying, and backbiting stain the heart

kartlar.icerik:
The Quran praises the people of taqwa as those who restrain their anger and forgive others. The Messenger of Allah also repeatedly advised, 'Do not become angry.'

Feeling anger is not a sin, but failing to manage it and allowing it to control one's speech, actions, and decisions causes great harm. Good character does not mean denying the emotion; it means managing it in a way that pleases Allah.

When angry, it is helpful to remain silent, step away for a while, perform wudu, avoid making an immediate decision, and delay giving a hurtful response.

Sources: Al Imran 3:134; Bukhari 6116.
kartlar.vurgu: Strength lies in managing anger, not in venting it

kartlar.baslik: Forgiving and Responding to Evil with Good
kartlar.icerik:
The Quran teaches that evil and good are not equal and advises repelling evil with the best conduct. It states that, by acting this way, even someone who harbors enmity may become a close friend.

Forgiving does not mean completely giving up one's rights in every situation. But aiming to reform, soften hearts, and mend hurt rather than escalating revenge is a high level of good character. In particular, not becoming harsh out of personal ambition is a sign of great maturity.

Source: Fussilat 41:34.
kartlar.vurgu: Responding to evil with good is among the highest levels of character

kartlar.icerik:
In Surah Luqman, people are commanded not to turn their faces away from others or walk arrogantly on the earth. Arrogance leads a person to think highly of themselves and look down on others.

Humility, however, does not mean seeing oneself as worthless. It means recognizing the blessings Allah has given without using them to look down on others. A person of good character does not hurt others by boasting about their knowledge, worship or means.

Source: Luqman 31:18.
kartlar.vurgu: Humility makes a person beautiful; arrogance darkens the heart

kartlar.baslik: Dignity, Moderation and Tone of Voice
kartlar.icerik:
The Quran teaches moderation in walking and avoiding raising one's voice unnecessarily. Good character is reflected not only in major decisions but also in how one walks, sits and speaks, including one's tone and manner.

Harshness and shouting often do not strengthen a valid point; instead, they make one's words unpleasant. A dignified believer does not make noise to draw attention to themselves. Calmness, balance and moderation are among the outward expressions of good character.

Sources: Luqman 31:19; Abu Dawud 4776.
kartlar.vurgu: Good character calls for moderation in speech, walking and conduct

kartlar.icerik:
The Messenger of Allah said that the Most Merciful will show mercy to those who show mercy, and that the One in heaven will show mercy to anyone who shows mercy to those on earth.

Mercy is not merely feeling pity; it is recognizing another's need and treating them kindly. Showing gentleness at home, at work and in the street, and toward animals, children and the vulnerable, is among the essential signs of good character.

Mercilessness hardens the heart. Mercy brings a person closer both to their Lord and to His servants.

Source: Tirmidhi 1924.
kartlar.vurgu: Those who show mercy are shown mercy

kartlar.icerik:
The Prophet ﷺ said that the best of people are those who treat their families best. True character is tested by whether one is kind outside the home without being hurtful at home.

Respect for parents, kindness to one's spouse, compassion toward children and fairness at home are among the most important aspects of good character. Sometimes people behave most impulsively toward those they love most. Family life is therefore a test of the sincerity of one's character.

Source: Tirmidhi 3895.
kartlar.vurgu: The truest test of character is often within the home

kartlar.baslik: The Rights of Neighbors and Avoiding Harm to Others
kartlar.icerik:
The Messenger of Allah stated in striking terms that a person whose neighbor is not safe from their harm has a serious deficiency in their iman. Speaking good, avoiding harm to one's neighbor and honoring one's guest are also taught as requirements of iman.

Good character becomes visible in not placing a heavy burden on others, behaving respectfully in shared spaces, not disturbing others with loud noise, causing no material or emotional harm and observing the rights of neighbors.

Sources: Bukhari 6016; Bukhari 6475.
kartlar.vurgu: A believer is someone who gives their neighbors and those around them a sense of security

kartlar.icerik:
The Prophet ﷺ said that modesty is a part of iman. Modesty is a quality that helps a person feel a sense of shame before Allah, abandon what is unworthy of them and observe boundaries.

The Quran also commands people not to enter another person's home without asking permission and offering a greeting of peace. This is more than etiquette at the door; it teaches respect for personal space, privacy and consideration. Good character also includes respecting people's boundaries.

Sources: Bukhari 24; an-Nur 24:27.
kartlar.vurgu: Modesty is part of iman; respect for privacy is part of good character

kartlar.baslik: A Cheerful Face and Small Acts of Kindness
kartlar.icerik:
The Messenger of Allah counted even smiling at one's brother as charity. This shows that good character does not consist only of great sacrifices.

Removing something harmful from a path, giving someone directions, not dismissing a small act of help and treating people warmly rather than harshly are opportunities to show good character in daily life. Sometimes an act of kindness that seems small can win someone's heart in a big way.

Source: Tirmidhi 1956.
kartlar.vurgu: Do not underestimate small acts of kindness; even a smile is charity

kartlar.baslik: A Daily Roadmap for Developing Good Character
kartlar.icerik:
Good character does not develop in a day; it takes root through small, repeated choices. It is helpful to choose one area to work on each day: today I will watch my words, today I will remain silent when angry, or today I will treat my family more kindly.

Three steps are helpful in developing good character:

• Reflect on your conduct at the end of the day
• When you make a mistake, repent and make amends immediately
• Frequently remember the example of the Messenger of Allah

Acts of worship, supplication and righteous company strengthen good character. The goal is not to appear perfect, but to grow a little more mature each day.
kartlar.vurgu: Good character is strengthened through intentional repetition and self-reflection
